router/swap: In a transformer block, every token runs through the same MLP. A mixture of experts, or M O E, keeps several MLPs instead, called experts. Call their number E: here, four.
router/router: A router, one small linear layer and a softmax, gives each expert a probability for the current token: zero point one, zero point five, zero point one five and zero point two five.
router/top: Only the k most likely experts run, the top k. With k at two, that is experts one and three. The other two do no work for this token.
router/gates: Their probabilities add up to zero point seven five. Divide each by that total, and the gates become two thirds and one third, adding up to one again.
router/sum: The layer's output is two thirds of expert one's output, plus one third of expert three's.
balance/favor: One danger. Early in training, the router may happen to favor one expert.
balance/feed: That expert gets more tokens, so more gradient, so it improves fastest, and the router favors it even more.
balance/collapse: Soon one expert does most of the work. The others sit idle: parameters stored and paid for, barely trained. And the busy one makes the whole layer wait.
balance/fix: The fix is a small extra loss that is lowest when every expert gets an equal share of the tokens: one over E each.
params/count: Now count parameters. Say a layer has eight experts of a hundred million parameters each, and k is two.
params/total: All eight must be stored, since the next token might need any of them: eight hundred million. That is the total.
params/active: But one token runs only two of them: two hundred million. That is the active count, and it sets the compute per token.
params/grow: Double the experts to sixteen, and the total doubles while the active count stays put. The model can store more, at the same work per token.
model/layers: A whole model stacks many such layers, each with its own experts. Say four layers, each with eight experts of a hundred million, and k still two.
model/shared: Everything else, attention, embeddings and the rest, is shared: every token uses it, and it is stored once. Say five hundred million.
model/active: One token runs two experts in each of four layers: four times two times a hundred million, eight hundred million. Add the shared five hundred: thirteen hundred million active.
model/total: The model stores all eight in every layer: four times eight times a hundred million, thirty two hundred million. Plus the shared five hundred: thirty seven hundred million in total.
